Sellside Analysts' Memo · Hellenic Telecom · built 2 November 2026

How the sell-side sees Hellenic Telecom, and where its view is heading

What each broker on record thinks and how that has moved over twelve months, with the Investment Analyst's judgement on where the sell-side goes next.

  • Three kinds of content, each labelled. The brokers' own commentary, from 34 research reports produced between 3 Jun 2026 and 29 Oct 2026 (blue-edged cards). The Investment Analyst's reading of the sell-side, from its Layers 1 to 4 and three memos (purple-edged cards and the judgement boxes). This memo's summaries, tables and charts, which name their sources.
  • Names. OTE is the company's own name: the Hellenic Telecommunications Organisation, listed as Hellenic Telecom.
  • Breadth. 1144 passages from 13 research houses, plus consensus and investor views. Every house the research records on this stock is included, however briefly it appears.
  • Checks. Every quotation was matched word for word to its source by script, every summary sentence was checked against the passages, and every number survived the editing.
How current this is, and what was left out

The research passages come from AlphaSense reports produced between 3 June and 29 October 2026 and record broker views dated from 2015 to 26 October 2026 (481 of the 490 dated views are from June 2024 onward); the latest views on OTE itself are Morgan Stanley's notes of 23 and 25 October 2026, and the latest broker note title is Morgan Stanley's Risk Reward Update of 16 September 2026. The Investment Analyst's current work was written on 27 and 28 October 2026 from FactSet and dashboard data as at 27 October 2026, and it dates the third-quarter results to 30 October 2026, which none of these inputs cover; the summary also draws on its earlier memos of 4 July and 26 September 2026.

No passage carries the April to May 2026 stale-research flag, so nothing was excluded on that ground. Passages about other operators (Elisa, Swisscom, KPN, Digi, Telekom Austria) are used only where the research applies them to OTE, and two passages whose text names no house (one tagged to NBG Securities, one tagged to Deutsche Bank) are not attributed to those houses. Where a research report draws its own conclusion from a broker's fact (typically a sentence opening "This means" or "Consequently"), the summary credits that conclusion to the report, not to the broker.

The answer in brief

  1. Thirteen houses on FactSet, but the written research is two houses deep.

    • Thirteen houses cover OTE on FactSet, nine of them with earnings per share estimates, according to the Investment Analyst's reading of 27 October 2026.
    • Deutsche Bank (530 passages) and Morgan Stanley (478 passages) dominate the AlphaSense research; the Investment Analyst calls the narrative "two houses deep", noting that the narrative report it read credits views only to Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank and Bernstein.
    • Eleven other houses add between one and 24 passages each, mostly on the sector or on Greece: Bernstein, Axia Ventures, Jefferies, NBG Securities, ING, DNB Carnegie, Norne Securities, JPMorgan, Rothschild & Co Redburn, Ambit Capital and Guotai Junan.
    • The FactSet buy share is 54%, down 15 points over both three and six months (read 27 October 2026), against 65% Overweight in Refinitiv data collated by Morgan Stanley (recorded in a report of 3 June 2026), a different data source.
    • Most positive are Morgan Stanley (Overweight, highest target €23.80, 16 September 2026) and Deutsche Bank (Buy, €23.00, last reiterated in May 2026), although FactSet has shown Deutsche Bank's rating as Without since 23 October 2026 (see conflicts).
    • Least positive are Barclays (Sell, €18.00, 19 October 2026) and Eurobank (Hold, €17.50, 14 September 2026), both visible only on FactSet, with JPMorgan at Neutral and €20.00 as of late 2025; the Investment Analyst counts four other houses at Hold on FactSet without naming them.
    Source: Investment Analyst (Layer 1; Layers 3 and 4) reading FactSet; FactSet revisions of 27 October 2026; AlphaSense research passages.

  2. Headlines were most bullish from February to May 2026 and have cooled since July.

    • Over twelve months, note titles moved from Morgan Stanley's initiation, "A New OTE is Here: Initiate OW" (29 October 2025; OW means Overweight), to Deutsche Bank's titles of February and March 2026.
    • Deutsche Bank's February and March 2026 titles were "4Q FY25 #s v. good; FY26 guide ahead of DBe" (26 February 2026: fourth-quarter 2025 numbers very good and 2026 guidance ahead of Deutsche Bank's estimates) and "Bullish incremental news" (17 March 2026).
    • In the last six months, titles stayed upbeat into May: Morgan Stanley's "Top-line ahead, MSR growth very strong" (8 May 2026; MSR means mobile service revenue) and Deutsche Bank's "PPC is unlikely to bid for spectrum" (22 May 2026; PPC is the utility Public Power Corporation).
    • In the last three months, the only titles are Morgan Stanley's: "Top-line weakness driven by phase-out of Int'l Wholesale" (29 July 2026) and a "Risk Reward Update" (16 September 2026) that raised Morgan Stanley's target.
    • The note ledger records no Deutsche Bank title on OTE after 22 May 2026, and over the last three months the FactSet buy share fell 15 points to 54%.
    Source: Brokers' note titles (Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley); FactSet via the Investment Analyst.

  3. Morgan Stanley raised its target four times; Deutsche Bank last moved in February; low end €17.50 to €18.00.

    • Morgan Stanley initiated at Overweight with a €20.00 target in October 2025, then raised it to €20.70 in January 2026, €21.40 in April 2026 and €21.50 on 12 May 2026.
    • Morgan Stanley raised its target to €23.80 on 16 September 2026 (+11%); a revision table (report of 25 September 2026) gives the reason as "lowered market risk premium from 8% to 7%".
    • Deutsche Bank's Buy target went from €19.50 in mid-2025 to €21.00 in November 2025, then up 10% to €23.00 on 27 February 2026 ("Price Target raised 10% to +30% vs. last close").
    • Deutsche Bank's John Karidis reiterated Buy and €23.00 on 8 and 11 May 2026, although one passage dates the €23.00 target to April 2026 (see conflicts); Axia Ventures' Buy at €19.50 and JPMorgan's Neutral at €20.00 both date from 2025.
    • The low end comes from FactSet only: Eurobank at Hold with €17.50 (14 September 2026) and Barclays at Sell with €18.00 (19 October 2026); a €17.50 low target was already recorded in reports of 3 and 19 June 2026.
    • FactSet's mean target is €20.92 and its median €21.20 (27 October 2026), with consensus target revisions of 0% over one month, (1)% over three months and +4% over six months.
    Source: AlphaSense research passages; brokers' note titles; FactSet via the Investment Analyst; FactSet revisions.

  4. The sharpest shift: the threat moved from the utility's failed retail discounts to the Vodafone fibre venture.

    • Before the first-quarter results, the sell-side bar was set low on fear of a utility-led price war; post-results broker notes were dominated by "absolute relief that the Public Power Corporation was not entering the mobile market" (recorded in a report of 7 June 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank's Karidis framed the utility as a failed retail entrant, with fewer than 11,000 broadband subscribers by the end of 2025 (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
    • After the second quarter, Morgan Stanley noted mobile service revenue growth slowing to 2.3% from 5.5%, and retail fixed service revenue growth flat at 0.3% (29 July 2026).
    • The Vodafone Greece and Public Power Corporation fibre venture is now the threat: Morgan Stanley warned on 16 September 2026 that a monetised venture would be a "highly formidable competitor", and on 14 October 2026 NBG Securities called the venture "a major threat to OTE".
    • The Investment Analyst says the narrative has turned from "new OTE" to "watch the venture".
    Source: AlphaSense research passages (Developments summary, Earnings Review, Key Question research); Investment Analyst memo.

  5. Agreed: the utility's retail push has failed. Split: how much wholesale revenue the fibre venture will take.

    • Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley agree that Public Power Corporation's broadband has barely dented OTE, despite being priced about 50% below the incumbents; JPMorgan is more cautious on near-term retail broadband pricing pressure from the utility (recorded in a report of 25 September 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank puts the utility at fewer than 11,000 retail broadband customers by the end of 2025 (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026); other passages credit Deutsche Bank with 18,000 to 20,000 (see conflicts).
    • Morgan Stanley puts the utility at about 13,000 retail broadband customers despite 1.7 million premises passed (recorded in a report of 17 August 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank says wholesale discounts of up to 28% bind Vodafone Greece and Nova to OTE's network, and on 17 March 2026 called fibre overbuild in Greece immaterial.
    • Morgan Stanley warned on 21 April 2026 that OTE could lose up to €250 million of high-margin wholesale sales if competitors move their volume quickly, and that Vodafone Greece and Nova have strong incentives to shift traffic to their own networks once built.
    • A report of 28 October 2026 draws a "structural wholesale revenue cliff" within three years from Morgan Stanley's warning; on 16 September 2026 Morgan Stanley argued that the venture also eases overbuild worries by merging build plans.
    • ING reported on 10 June 2026 that the venture involves about €130 million of cash paid to the utility, which the report citing ING reads as meaning "the venture will accelerate fiber overbuild".
    • Bernstein (12 June 2025) cited Italy as showing that utility-backed overbuild can compress incumbents' wholesale revenues over three to five years, and Ireland, where the utility-backed SIRO network drew retail tenants to compete with the incumbent Eir.
    Source: AlphaSense research passages for Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, ING and Bernstein.

    The wholesale revenue at risk from the venture

    Morgan Stanley warns OTE could lose up to €250 million of high-margin wholesale sales if Vodafone Greece and Nova move their volume to their own networks quickly.

  6. Agreed: pricing power is the bull case. Doubts: the second-quarter slowdown and the European court ruling.

    • All three Greek mobile operators raised prices with inflation for a second consecutive year, Deutsche Bank records (17 February 2026), and Morgan Stanley (21 April 2026) records inflation-linked rises by all three over the prior year.
    • Deutsche Bank values each prepaid-to-postpaid migration at €3 to €4 a month of average revenue per user.
    • Morgan Stanley's base case rests on about 3% long-term mobile service revenue growth (16 September 2026), yet that growth slowed to 2.3% in the second quarter from 5.5% in the first (29 July 2026).
    • The European Court of Justice ruling forced Vodafone Germany to reverse a €5 monthly broadband price rise, as Morgan Stanley highlighted on 14 September 2026; on 16 September 2026 Deutsche Bank said the ruling blocks operators from changing contracts unilaterally even when customers may leave without penalty.
    • A report of 28 October 2026 that records both views reads the ruling as "a critical threat to OTE's future tariff adjustments", and says OTE's December indexation clauses "could face devastating challenges" if Greek consumer bodies use the precedent.
    • No house applies the court ruling to Greek contracts, the Investment Analyst notes.
    • Morgan Stanley noted on 16 September 2026 that the size of the December 2026 price step "remains unconfirmed"; the same 28 October 2026 report records that both houses, Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley, "assign low probability to immediate Greek regulatory intervention".
    Source: AlphaSense research passages for Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley; Investment Analyst (Layers 3 and 4).

  7. Agreed: 2026 growth leans on front-loaded public information technology work. Split: whether 2027 brings a cliff.

    • Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley both cautioned on 26 February 2026 that OTE's 3% EBITDAaL growth for 2026 relies on front-loaded public information and communications technology projects funded by the Recovery and Resilience Facility, which ends in December 2026.
    • Morgan Stanley argues the Greek economy faces no investment cliff because of a lag of one to two years between receiving and using the funds (21 April, 22 May and 6 July 2026).
    • Jefferies reported on 8 September 2026 that only €6.4 billion of Greece's €17.7 billion recovery loan allocation had been disbursed, a delayed pipeline that the report citing Jefferies says "could prevent a sudden collapse in corporate capital expenditure".
    • Deutsche Bank noted on 24 April 2026 that clients are rushing to use the funds before the deadline, from which the report citing Deutsche Bank infers a significant fall in public-sector revenue in the final quarters of 2026.
    • Deutsche Bank also warns that information and communications technology revenue may contract for a period after 2026 if private demand does not replace public work quickly enough (recorded in a report of 14 September 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley itself noted System Solutions growth slowing from 76.3% to 52.1% between the first and second quarters (29 July 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank's forecasts have other fixed revenue, mostly information and communications technology, rising from €996 million in 2026 to €1,124 million in 2028 (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
    Source: AlphaSense research passages for Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley and Jefferies.

  8. Estimates rose once, with the February 2026 guidance, and have been flat since.

    • FactSet consensus for financial year 2027 (read 27 October 2026) shows earnings per share revisions of +3% over twelve months, (1)% over six months and 0% over three months and one month.
    • FactSet 2027 EBITDA revisions are +2%, 0%, +1% and 0% over twelve, six, three and one months, and sales revisions (5)%, (1)%, +1% and 0%, the twelve-month fall reflecting the transit exit, according to the Investment Analyst.
    • Consensus earnings per share stands at €1.64 for 2026, €1.70 for 2027, €1.81 for 2028 and €1.91 for 2029 (one broker); the 2026 figure is +5.3% over twelve months and (0.8)% over six months, and the 2028 figure (2.2)% over six months.
    • Brokers diverge most on 2027 revenue: Deutsche Bank's note of 8 May 2026 had €3,379.1 million after removing the transit, down from €3,463 million in its note of 13 November 2025.
    • Morgan Stanley had 2027 revenue of €3,619 million on 21 April 2026 without removing the transit, against a FactSet consensus of €3,495 million.
    • The Investment Analyst summarises the record: "Upgrades came once, with the February 2026 guide; since then flat with a slight downward drift at the far end."
    Source: FactSet revisions of 27 October 2026; Investment Analyst (Layer 1; memo); AlphaSense research passages.

  9. Both main houses call the valuation discount unjustified, and their targets assume it narrows.

    • Deutsche Bank puts OTE at 5.0x enterprise value to EBITDAaL, 23% below the 6.5x sector average, with an 8.3% equity free cash flow yield (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
    • Even Deutsche Bank's €23.00 target implies 6.2x, a report of 27 October 2026 adds, which "would still represent a 5% discount to European peers".
    • Morgan Stanley put OTE's discount to the European telecom average at 37% in October 2025, and raised its target to €23.80 after cutting its cost of capital from 10.1% to 9.4% (September 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley stresses a 2027 shareholder return yield of 8.5% against a 3.7% Greek ten-year bond yield (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026 and in its note of 16 September 2026).
    • A report of 28 October 2026 sets OTE's roughly 5.0x forward enterprise value to EBITDA against the roughly 10.0x that DNB Carnegie gave for Elisa on 5 October 2026, calling the gap "a structural discount of approximately 50% against its Nordic peer group".
    • Caution from Bernstein: a 100 basis point rise in risk-free rates cuts telecom target valuations by 18% on average, Bernstein estimates (19 October 2026).
    • Caution from Barclays: Barclays' Sell at €18.00 is, in the Investment Analyst's reading, a call on valuation rather than earnings; the Investment Analyst's September 2026 memo adds that "the sell-side raised targets on the multiple" rather than on earnings.
    Source: AlphaSense research passages for Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, DNB Carnegie and Bernstein; Investment Analyst (Layer 1; September memo).

    Targets rose on the multiple, not on earnings

    Both main houses call OTE's valuation discount unjustified, but the Investment Analyst notes the sell-side raised targets on the multiple rather than on earnings.

  10. Investors' focus: index flows, the fibre venture and a falling buy share.

    • Morgan Stanley recorded a 6% fall in OTE's shares in January 2026, as investors feared OTE would fail MSCI's size and liquidity rules for Developed Market indices (21 April 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley found only 12% of European active long-only funds held any Greek equities (21 September 2026), and put OTE's pro-forma MSCI Europe weight at 0.02% but its net passive inflows at 63 million US dollars (25 September 2026).
    • Before the second-quarter results, the market's focus was Greek mobile momentum and the Vodafone and Public Power Corporation fibre venture (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
    • A report of 28 October 2026 headlines "Fading analyst optimism" as buy ratings fell 15 points to 54%.
    • Hedge fund net exposure was "only 4.7%" with no short-seller reports (recorded in a report of 19 June 2026), and the Investment Analyst found no buy-side or forum commentary in the files beyond Greek business press and expert calls.
    Source: AlphaSense research passages for Morgan Stanley and on investors; FactSet via the research; Investment Analyst (Layers 3 and 4).

  11. The Investment Analyst's judgement: sentiment turned first, and a cut to the numbers is due in February 2027.

    • The Investment Analyst judges that consensus will be held through the third-quarter results and cut at the full-year results in February 2027.
    • The Investment Analyst's expected 2027 cuts are: revenue by 3% to 6%, EBITDA by 1% to 2% and earnings per share by 2% to 3%.
    • The Investment Analyst puts the chance that consensus 2027 earnings per share is lower in a year at about 60%, higher at about 20% and unchanged at about 20%.
    • The Investment Analyst reads the falling buy share alongside flat estimates as "a sentiment-first, numbers-second sequence", and concludes that "even the bull case produces a held consensus, not an upgrade cycle".
    • The Investment Analyst's central difference with the brokers is its view that OTE's core business, stripped of the price step and public information technology work, is flat to shrinking, which it says appears in no broker document.
    Source: Investment Analyst (Layers 3 and 4; memo draft).

    The Investment Analyst expects a February 2027 cut

    The Investment Analyst puts about 60% odds on lower 2027 consensus earnings per share in a year, with cuts of 2% to 3% expected at the February 2027 results.

Where the sell-side's view is heading

The Investment Analyst's judgement

The Investment Analyst judges OTE is no longer an upgrade story: sentiment turned first, and a cut to 2027 estimates comes with February's guidance.

  • Twelve months: one upgrade, then flat. 2027 consensus earnings per share rose 3% and EBITDA 2%, while sales fell 5% as transit was partly removed; the one upgrade came with the February 2026 guidance.
  • Six, three and one month: sentiment moved first. Earnings per share moved (1)%, 0% and 0%, but the buy share fell 15 points over three months to 54%; the Investment Analyst calls this sentiment first, numbers second.
  • Targets and ratings: consensus target price rose 4% over six months, slipped (1)% over three and was flat over one; on 25 September no broker rated OTE Sell, and Barclays' Sell is dated 19 October.
  • What turned it: the Investment Analyst records the narrative cooling on the second-quarter revenue miss and mobile deceleration and turning from "new OTE" to "watch the venture"; Orange Polska and Telekom Austria took OTE's upgrade role.
  • Where next: held, then cut. The Investment Analyst expects consensus held through the third-quarter results, then cut in February 2027: 2027 EBITDA by about 1% to 2%, earnings per share by 2% to 3%.
  • Why: the Investment Analyst expects a 2027 guide of about +1% to +2% against the street's +3%, as the December price step must carry 2027 just when Recovery and Resilience Facility work falls away.
  • What would prove it wrong: the Investment Analyst puts about 20% on consensus rising instead: a December price step of 4% or more, a 2027 guide of about +3%, or a 2027 distribution above 600 EURm.

What each broker says

Each research house in turn, ordered by how much the research records from it: its view in one line, then how it frames the case, its arguments, its worries and how its view changed. Quoted words are the research report's.

Deutsche BankJohn Karidis (one report of 3 June 2026 also names Robert Grindle, Keval Khiroya, Roshan Ranjit, Vijay Saravanan and Ankit Sharma; see conflicts)Buy, target €23.00 (reiterated 8 and 11 May 2026); FactSet shows the rating as Without since 23 October 2026 (see conflicts)

Deutsche Bank rates OTE Buy at €23.00 and frames it as the dominant, under-levered Greek incumbent at an unjustified discount, though FactSet has shown Without since 23 October 2026.

Stance and how it got there

  • Deutsche Bank's stance now is Buy, €23.00. Deutsche Bank initiated on OTE with a Buy on 3 March 2015, and every Deutsche Bank rating recorded in the research since then is Buy.
  • Deutsche Bank's target rose from €19.50 in mid-2025 to €21.00 in November 2025, then 10% to €23.00 on 27 February 2026 after the 2025 results, which John Karidis tied to a 6% rise in his yearly free cash flow estimates.
  • Deutsche Bank's Karidis reiterated Buy and €23.00 on 8 and 11 May 2026 and left his forecasts unchanged after the first quarter, even though 4.9% revenue growth beat his 0.0% forecast.
  • The note ledger has no Deutsche Bank title on OTE after 22 May 2026. FactSet has shown Deutsche Bank's rating as Without since 23 October 2026, while, according to the Investment Analyst, Deutsche Bank's own publication that day kept an unchanged May Buy.

How it frames the case

  • Deutsche Bank frames OTE as the dominant, under-levered Greek incumbent, with over 65% of market revenue and 73% of EBITDA after leases (December 2024), trading at an unjustified discount.
  • Deutsche Bank puts OTE at 5.0x enterprise value to EBITDAaL, 23% below the 6.5x sector average, with an 8.3% equity free cash flow yield (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank's Karidis argues that rivals Nova and Vodafone Greece cannot afford a price war because their operating cash flows are low or negative (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank's Karidis also argues that customers have consistently chosen value over low price because of OTE's high network quality (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).

Main arguments

  • On competition, Deutsche Bank says Public Power Corporation lacks a mobile network, a pay-television platform and a complete fibre network, and won fewer than 11,000 retail broadband customers by the end of 2025 (other passages credit Deutsche Bank with 18,000 to 20,000; see conflicts).
  • Deutsche Bank calls fibre overbuild in Greece immaterial (17 March 2026), and says wholesale discounts of up to 28% bind Vodafone Greece and Nova to OTE's network.
  • On cash, Deutsche Bank expects a €125 million Romanian tax break to cover about €78 million of 2027 spectrum renewals, leaving €47 million of exceptional free cash flow (16 February 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank sees scope for capital expenditure to fall toward €550 million by 2029 and €520 million in 2030, although other passages have Deutsche Bank modelling a flat €600 million a year through 2028 or 2029 (see conflicts).
  • On pricing, Deutsche Bank records all three operators raising prices with inflation for a second year in early 2026, and values each prepaid-to-postpaid migration at €3 to €4 a month.

What worries it

  • Deutsche Bank cautioned on 26 February 2026 that the 3% EBITDAaL growth for 2026 relies on front-loaded public information and communications technology work, and warns that this revenue may contract for a period after 2026 if private demand does not replace it quickly enough.
  • Deutsche Bank's Karidis noted national wholesale revenue falling €15 million in 2025 as rivals moved customers to their own lines; the report citing him (27 October 2026) adds that faster rival builds would bring sustained long-term revenue erosion.
  • Deutsche Bank said on 16 September 2026 that the European Court of Justice ruling blocks operators from changing contracts unilaterally, which a report of 28 October 2026 reads as meaning OTE's December indexation clauses could face devastating challenges.
  • Deutsche Bank warned on 17 November 2025 that Greek inflation could trigger consumer pushback or government intervention.

How its view changed

  • Since October 2025, Deutsche Bank's notes moved from one on meeting the utility as Greece's price disruptor (20 October 2025) to Bullish incremental news (17 March 2026) and a 10% higher target.
  • Over six months, Deutsche Bank held its Buy and forecasts after the first quarter.
  • Deutsche Bank's note of 8 May 2026 had 2027 revenue of €3,379.1 million with the transit removed (down from €3,463 million in its note of 13 November 2025) and 2027 EBITDA of €1,491 million.
  • Over three months, the recorded Deutsche Bank views are on Greece and the sector rather than on OTE directly: the Greek index move and Greek valuations (4 September), the court ruling (16 September) and Vodafone's €20 million provision (30 September).
  • Also over three months, Deutsche Bank noted FiberCop's shortfall of 1.6 million lines in Italy (12 October 2026), which a report reads as a sign the venture may miss its targets; there is no new Deutsche Bank company note in the ledger.

Morgan StanleyLindsey Zastawny (lead), with Emmet Kelly; one report of 3 June 2026 also names Terence Tsui and Harrison Williams (see conflicts)Overweight, target €23.80 (16 September 2026), the highest on FactSet; a report reads its third-quarter preview of 23 October 2026 as reinforcing the Overweight

Morgan Stanley is Overweight with the street-high €23.80 target, framing OTE as a clean Greek pure-play with a cash-based return case, while warning about the fibre venture.

Stance and how it got there

  • Morgan Stanley's stance now is Overweight, €23.80, the street high. Morgan Stanley initiated on 29 October 2025 with A New OTE is Here: Initiate OW (Overweight) and a €20.00 target.
  • Lindsey Zastawny raised Morgan Stanley's target to €20.70 in January 2026, to €21.40 in April 2026 on a higher mid-term outlook for System Solutions, and to €21.50 on 12 May 2026 after the first quarter.
  • Morgan Stanley's target went to €23.80 on 16 September 2026 after rolling the model forward and lowering the market risk premium from 8% to 7%, which cut the cost of capital from 10.1% to 9.4%.
  • Morgan Stanley kept Overweight and €21.50 after the second quarter (29 July 2026), and its preview of 23 October 2026 expects third-quarter revenue of €883 million and EBITDAaL of €366 million.

How it frames the case

  • Morgan Stanley frames OTE as a clean Greek pure-play after the Romanian exit of 1 October 2025, with the best mobile network quality in Greece for ten consecutive years.
  • Morgan Stanley's framing includes mobile service revenue growth of about 2.9% a year to 2030 from data growth and prepaid-to-postpaid migration, and leverage of 0.2x to 0.3x net debt to EBITDA against 2.4x for European peers.
  • Morgan Stanley's return case is cash: a 2027 shareholder return yield of 8.5% against a 3.7% Greek ten-year bond yield, and payouts reaching 98% of free cash flow by 2030.
  • Buybacks supply about 3.2 points of Morgan Stanley's 7.1% earnings per share growth for 2026 (12 May 2026); Morgan Stanley put OTE's discount to the European telecom average at 37% in October 2025.

Main arguments

  • Morgan Stanley argues the end of the Recovery and Resilience Facility brings no investment cliff for the Greek economy, because of a lag of one to two years in using the funds (21 April, 22 May and 6 July 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley explained the second-quarter revenue miss as the planned transit exit, with underlying revenue up 8% (29 July 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley estimates the utility won only about 13,000 active retail customers despite 1.7 million premises passed (recorded in a report of 17 August 2026), and says OTE's re-contracting has limited churn (21 April 2026).

What worries it

  • Morgan Stanley warned on 21 April 2026 that up to €250 million of high-margin wholesale sales are at risk if competitors move their volume quickly, and that Vodafone Greece and Nova have strong incentives to shift traffic to their own networks.
  • A report of 28 October 2026 draws a structural wholesale revenue cliff within three years from Morgan Stanley's warning of 21 April 2026.
  • Morgan Stanley said on 16 September 2026 that a monetised Vodafone Greece and Public Power Corporation venture would be a highly formidable competitor, although the same note says the venture eases overbuild worries by merging build plans.
  • Morgan Stanley highlighted the European Court of Justice ruling against Vodafone Germany's price rise (14 September 2026), which a report of 28 October 2026 reads as a threat to OTE's price rises.
  • Morgan Stanley's Zastawny calls falling real purchasing power a key risk downplayed by consensus (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley's bear case of €15.20 (12 May and 16 September 2026) assumes 4.5x enterprise value to EBITDA, the 20th percentile of OTE's history; in January 2026 its bull and bear values were €29.50 and €14.60.

How its view changed

  • Over twelve months, Morgan Stanley moved from initiation to four target rises, from €20.00 to €23.80.
  • Over six months, Morgan Stanley's note titles went from a first quarter with very strong mobile service revenue growth (8 May 2026) to Top-line weakness driven by phase-out of Int'l Wholesale (29 July 2026), as mobile service revenue growth slowed to 2.3% from 5.5%.
  • Over three months, Morgan Stanley raised its target 11%, citing a model roll-forward and a lower market risk premium, while warning about the venture and highlighting the court ruling.

BernsteinNo rating or target on OTE recorded; sector research (Bernstein downgraded the parent, Deutsche Telekom, to Market-Perform on 24 September 2026)

Bernstein has no recorded rating or target on OTE; the reports apply its sector research on utility overbuild, risk-free rates and inflation indexation to OTE.

How it frames the case

  • Bernstein's 24 passages are sector research that the reports apply to OTE; no Bernstein rating or target on OTE is recorded.

Main arguments

  • Bernstein's report of 12 June 2025 cites Italy, where Open Fiber used the electricity company ENEL's network, as showing that utility overbuilds can compress wholesale revenues over three to five years.
  • Bernstein's report of 12 June 2025 also cites Ireland, where the utility-backed SIRO network drew retail tenants to compete with the incumbent Eir, and places Greece among countries whose high rollout costs reduce the risk of overbuild.
  • Bernstein's view, added by a report of 18 August 2026, is that mature utility fibre entrants refrain from permanent disruptive pricing once scale is achieved.
  • Bernstein says European regulators eased price constraints to allow front-book and back-book inflation indexation (24 September 2026).
  • Bernstein noted a 6.8% cost of capital for Deutsche Telekom's Greek division in August 2026.

What worries it

  • Bernstein estimates that a 100 basis point rise in the risk-free rate would deliver an average 18% hit to target valuations (October 2026).
  • Bernstein expects single-country telecoms in high risk-free rate markets to face persistent valuation pressure, although a report notes that OTE's clean balance sheet limits its direct exposure.
  • Bernstein warned on 23 January 2025 that diverging front-book and back-book tariffs leave operators exposed as indexation slows.
  • Bernstein warned on 24 September 2026 that operators often destroy value expanding into low-margin information technology services.

What worries it

Where the brokers disagree

Will the Vodafone Greece and Public Power Corporation fibre venture take OTE's wholesale revenue?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank says fibre overbuild in Greece is immaterial (17 March 2026), and that wholesale discounts of up to 28% bind Vodafone Greece and Nova to OTE's network.
  • Deutsche Bank reported FiberCop's shortfall of 1.6 million lines in Italy (12 October 2026), which a report reads as a sign the venture may miss its targets.
  • Morgan Stanley (16 September 2026) argues the venture eases overbuild worries by merging build plans.
  • A report citing NBG Securities (14 October 2026) names the competition review as the main hurdle to the targeted first-half 2027 closing, so prolonged scrutiny would defer the pressure.

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley warned on 21 April 2026 that up to €250 million of high-margin wholesale sales are at risk if competitors move their volume quickly, which a report reads as a wholesale revenue cliff within three years.
  • Morgan Stanley called a monetised venture a highly formidable competitor on 16 September 2026, and NBG Securities (14 October 2026) calls the venture a major threat that lets wholesale clients bypass OTE's network.
  • A report reads ING's account of the venture's €130 million cash payment (10 June 2026) as meaning the venture will accelerate overbuild.
  • Bernstein (12 June 2025) cites Italy as showing that utility-backed overbuild can compress incumbents' wholesale revenues over three to five years, alongside Ireland's utility-backed SIRO network.

Does the end of the Recovery and Resilience Facility in December 2026 cause an information technology revenue cliff in 2027?

The more positive side

  • Morgan Stanley argues there is no investment cliff for the Greek economy, because of a lag of one to two years between receiving and using the funds (21 April, 22 May and 6 July 2026).
  • Only 56% of the Recovery and Resilience Facility funds had been used by late 2025 (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Jefferies reported slow loan disbursement (8 June 2026), which a report reads as keeping projects producing revenue through 2027, and reported a €23 billion National Development Programme to sustain spending (8 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank expects maintenance revenue and international and private work to cushion the segment (24 April 2026).

The more negative side

  • Deutsche Bank noted on 24 April 2026 that clients are rushing to use the funds before the deadline, which a report reads as a significant fall in public-sector revenue in the final quarters of 2026.
  • Deutsche Bank warns that information technology revenue may contract for a period after 2026 if private demand is slow to replace public work (recorded in a report of 14 September 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley noted System Solutions growth slowing from 76.3% to 52.1% between the first and second quarters (29 July 2026).
  • Jefferies (10 September 2025) put Greece's facility at about 16% of gross domestic product, against 5% for the European Union average.

Is the second-quarter 2026 slowdown in mobile and retail fixed revenue temporary?

The more positive side

  • Morgan Stanley put underlying second-quarter revenue growth at 8% once the transit exit is stripped out (29 July 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley's analyst said cost execution supported the Overweight and that 62,000 fibre net additions reassured the buy-side (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
  • A report of 11 September 2026 reads the sell-side analysis as confirming the top-line weakness is transitory.
  • Deutsche Bank expects continuing prepaid-to-postpaid migration, worth €3 to €4 a month per user, to support mobile revenue (24 April 2026).

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley reported mobile service revenue growth slowing to 2.3% from 5.5% and retail fixed revenue flat at 0.3% (29 July 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley notes its base case depends heavily on sustaining 3% mobile service revenue growth (16 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank's Karidis suggests consensus long-term retail revenue growth may be too optimistic (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026), and JPMorgan is more cautious on retail broadband pricing (recorded in a report of 25 September 2026).
  • FactSet shows buy ratings down 15 points to 54% (October 2026).

Can OTE keep raising prices with inflation after the European Court of Justice ruling?

The more positive side

  • All three Greek operators raised prices with inflation for a second consecutive year, Deutsche Bank records (17 February 2026), and Morgan Stanley (21 April 2026) records inflation-linked rises by all three over the prior year.
  • Morgan Stanley says OTE's network quality justifies higher pricing than budget rivals and limits subscriber pushback (16 September 2026).
  • Bernstein notes European regulators eased price constraints to allow front-book and back-book indexation (24 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley assign low probability to immediate Greek regulatory intervention, a report of 28 October 2026 records.

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley highlighted the court's ruling against a Vodafone Germany price rise (14 September 2026); Deutsche Bank said the ruling blocks unilateral contract changes (16 September 2026) and pointed to Vodafone's €20 million provision (30 September 2026).
  • A report of 28 October 2026 reads the ruling as a critical threat to OTE's tariff adjustments and says OTE's December indexation clauses could face devastating challenges.
  • Morgan Stanley notes the size of the December 2026 step is unconfirmed (16 September 2026), and Morgan Stanley's Zastawny warns consensus downplays falling real purchasing power (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank warned on 17 November 2025 that Greek inflation could trigger consumer pushback or government intervention.

Has the transit exit (130 million euros of zero-margin revenue in 2027) been taken out of 2027 revenue forecasts?

The more positive side

  • Morgan Stanley forecast 2027 revenue of €3,619 million and 2028 revenue of €3,708 million on 21 April 2026, with the transit exit not factored in.
  • Morgan Stanley expects revenue growth of about 2% a year to 2029 as System Solutions offsets wholesale declines (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley's 2027 adjusted EBITDA forecast of €1,503 million (16 September 2026) sits above the FactSet consensus of €1,489 million.

The more negative side

  • Deutsche Bank's 2027 revenue forecast fell from €3,463 million (13 November 2025) to €3,379.1 million (8 May 2026) as it removed the transit, with 2027 EBITDA of €1,491 million.
  • The Investment Analyst records Eurobank at €3,383 million for 2027 revenue.
  • FactSet's €3,495 million consensus lags the transit exit because several models still include it, a report of 28 October 2026 says.
  • The Investment Analyst judges consensus 2027 revenue about 6% too high, with no effect on EBITDA.

Is OTE's valuation discount to European telecoms unjustified?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank calls the discount unwarranted (recorded in a report of 19 June 2026) and puts OTE at 5.0x enterprise value to EBITDAaL, 23% below the 6.5x sector average, with an 8.3% equity free cash flow yield (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley put the discount at 37% (October 2025) and argues multiples do not reflect OTE's cash generation and low leverage (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Reports read DNB Carnegie's and Guotai Junan's data as support: a 50% discount to Elisa's multiple from DNB Carnegie's figure (5 October 2026), and a long re-rating path from Guotai Junan's KPN multiple (March 2024).
  • Reports also read the rising consensus dividend yield Norne Securities recorded (9 July 2026) as support for a re-rating.

The more negative side

  • Barclays rates OTE Sell at €18.00 (19 October 2026), which the Investment Analyst reads as a valuation call.
  • Bernstein expects single-country telecoms in high risk-free rate markets to face persistent valuation pressure (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank noted that Greek large caps remained among the cheapest in Europe on forward price to earnings (4 September 2026), which a report reads as having restricted OTE's multiple expansion.
  • A report draws from Norne Securities' July 2026 analysis that low leverage alone cannot guarantee a premium, and DNB Carnegie says the telecom earnings yield spread over government bonds has narrowed (26 October 2026).

Will Greece's move to Developed Market indices lift or weigh on the shares?

The more positive side

  • Morgan Stanley estimates net passive inflows into OTE of 63 million US dollars, about six days of trading volume (25 September 2026), which a report reads as a smooth transition.
  • Deutsche Bank's Karidis calls the upgrade a powerful structural catalyst (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026), and Jefferies argued it would lower the equity risk premium (23 June 2026).
  • Estimates of Greece's market-wide inflows from the May 2027 MSCI change differ (see conflicts).

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley puts OTE's pro-forma MSCI Europe weight at only 0.02% (25 September 2026), which a report reads as a risk of neglect.
  • Morgan Stanley recalls Greece underperforming for 10 to 11 months after its 2001 upgrade (25 November 2025), and recorded a 6% fall in January 2026 on index fears (21 April 2026).
  • Jefferies warned that Developed Market active funds often avoid very small constituents (5 February 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank warned that Emerging Market tracker outflows could outpace Developed Market buying at first (4 September 2026).

Will the 2027 distribution include the Romanian tax windfall?

The more positive side

  • Morgan Stanley says its distribution models may be too conservative and that OTE could distribute 100% of free cash flow (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley suggested in October 2025 that OTE could return the net proceeds of non-core sales as an extraordinary distribution.
  • Deutsche Bank notes OTE has no structural need to retain cash, which a report of 28 October 2026 reads as room to pay out the tax windfall and fund spectrum with debt.

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley expects the tax benefits to be kept for the 2027 spectrum renewal, leaving the distribution based on organic cash (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley warned on 29 October 2025 that the payout could fall if management retains cash to protect its credit profile.
  • Deutsche Bank expects the tax benefits to be fully allocated to spectrum and models €20 million a year of perpetual spectrum cost (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Analysts are divided, a report of 28 October 2026 says, and the Investment Analyst reads both Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley as assuming retention for spectrum.

Where the research reports conflict. Both versions are shown; this memo does not pick one.
  1. Deutsche Bank's current rating: Without on FactSet, or an unchanged Buy.
    • FactSet shows Deutsche Bank's rating as Without since 23 October 2026, in the Investment Analyst's Layer 1 reading; a report of 28 October 2026 says Deutsche Bank's rating changed that day for reasons it could not confirm.
    • The Investment Analyst's memo says Deutsche Bank's own publication of 23 October 2026 lists OTE with a stable A- credit rating and "an unchanged May Buy", so the change may be a restriction rather than a downgrade.
    • A report of 29 October 2026 says its findings "do not support the premise" that Deutsche Bank changed its rating that day, and that Deutsche Bank's latest detailed equity research, of 11 May 2026, reiterated Buy and €23.
    • No passage records a Deutsche Bank downgrade.
  2. Bear-case and stress values recorded alongside targets.
    • The Investment Analyst's broker list and the events file carry Morgan Stanley at €15.20, Axia Ventures at €14.40 and Deutsche Bank at €5.70; the Investment Analyst labels them as not targets, and the passages describe them as scenario values.
    • Morgan Stanley's €15.20 is its bear case (12 May and 16 September 2026, at 4.5x enterprise value to EBITDA), although one passage describes it as a cut to fair value on 16 September 2026.
    • Axia Ventures' €14.40 is a grey-sky case and Deutsche Bank's €5.70 a value under extreme currency stress (both recorded in a report of 19 June 2026); the same applies to Axia's €18.80 under pricing pressure.
    • The same also applies to Morgan Stanley's bull and bear values of €29.50 and €14.60 of 15 January 2026 and its 2015 Greek-exit values of €4.00 to €5.50 and €7.00; the recorded house targets are Morgan Stanley €23.80, Axia Ventures €19.50 and Deutsche Bank €23.00.
  3. When Deutsche Bank's target reached €23.00.
    • February 2026 version: several passages date Deutsche Bank's rise from €21.00 to €23.00 to February 2026, a revision table gives 27 February 2026, and Deutsche Bank's note title of that day reads "Price Target raised 10% to +30% vs. last close".
    • April 2026 version: a report of 27 October 2026 says Karidis raised Deutsche Bank's target from €19.50 in mid-2025 to €21.00 in November 2025 and eventually to €23.00 in April 2026.
    • Deutsche Bank's note title of 17 November 2025 says the target was "nudged up 5%", without giving the level it moved from.
    • A 5% rise to €21.00 implies a starting point of about €20.00, whereas the report of 27 October 2026 has Deutsche Bank's target moving from €19.50.
  4. Morgan Stanley's €23.80 in a passage dated to its report of 21 April 2026.
    • A report of 27 October 2026 gives Morgan Stanley's base-case target as €23.80 and its bearish value as €15.20 in a passage that opens with Morgan Stanley's report of 21 April 2026, without saying which Morgan Stanley report these come from.
    • The revision history in other passages has Morgan Stanley moving from €20.70 to €21.40 in April 2026, to €21.50 on 12 May 2026, and to €23.80 only on 16 September 2026.
  5. The September 2026 target range and median.
    • A report of 25 September 2026 gives a sell-side target range of €20.00 to €23.80 with a median of €23.00 at 14 September 2026.
    • The Investment Analyst's FactSet reading (latest estimate 16 September 2026) gives a range of €17.50 (Eurobank, Hold, 14 September 2026) to €23.80, a median of €21.20 and a mean of €20.97.
  6. The share of Buy ratings in September and October 2026.
    • Bloomberg consensus for September 2026 shows 75% Buy or Overweight, 25% Hold or Neutral and no Sell, as cited in a report of 25 September 2026.
    • Morgan Stanley's report of 16 September 2026 shows 59% Overweight, as cited in a report of 29 October 2026.
    • FactSet, as read by the Investment Analyst, shows a buy share of 64% on July 2026 data and 54% on 27 October 2026, with Barclays at Sell from 19 October 2026.
  7. Consensus earnings per share for 2026: €1.51 or €1.64.
    • Several passages give consensus earnings per share of €1.51 for 2026, €1.68 for 2027 and €1.83 for 2028.
    • One of those passages sources the €1.51, €1.68 and €1.83 consensus figures to Morgan Stanley's report of 16 September 2026, where the same 2026 and 2027 figures also appear as Morgan Stanley's own forecasts.
    • The Investment Analyst's FactSet median for 25 September 2026 is €1.64, €1.71 and €1.82, and FactSet on 27 October 2026 shows €1.64, €1.70 and €1.81.
    • 2026 estimates range from €1.51 to €1.84 because brokers treat a one-off tax benefit differently, the Investment Analyst notes.
  8. Morgan Stanley's earnings per share forecasts.
    • Reports of 27 and 28 October 2026 record Morgan Stanley's earnings per share as €1.51 for 2026 and €1.68 for 2027 (dated 16 September 2026), as €1.55 and €1.66, and as €1.53 and €1.66 after the first quarter.
    • A report of 11 September 2026 pairs Morgan Stanley's €21.50 target with an earnings per share path from €1.56 in 2025 to €1.75 in 2027, which matches Deutsche Bank's recorded forecasts rather than Morgan Stanley's recorded €1.23 for 2025.
  9. Public Power Corporation's customer count as attributed to Deutsche Bank.
    • Several passages cite Deutsche Bank for fewer than 11,000 retail broadband customers at Public Power Corporation by the end of 2025.
    • One report of 27 October 2026 cites Deutsche Bank for 18,000 connections by late 2025, and other passages cite Deutsche Bank for about 20,000 by early 2026 or at most 20,000 by March 2026.
    • Morgan Stanley's estimate is about 13,000 connected households (21 April 2026).
  10. Different analyst names for the same house.
    • Most passages name John Karidis as Deutsche Bank's analyst, but one report of 3 June 2026 says Roshan Ranjit, Vijay Saravanan and Ankit Sharma each hold the Buy and €23.00 target, and names Robert Grindle and Keval Khiroya as supporting analysts.
    • The same report of 3 June 2026 names Terence Tsui and Harrison Williams for Morgan Stanley alongside Lindsey Zastawny and Emmet Kelly.
    • For Axia Ventures, the same report names Stathis Kaparis (Buy set at his 2025 initiation), Alexis Chaidopoulos (Buy as of June 2025) and Constantinos Zouzoulas, although the note ledger shows Axia Ventures titles on OTE from 7 August 2024.
  11. Net passive inflows into Greece from the May 2027 MSCI reclassification: 0.9 or 0.6 billion US dollars.
    • Two passages in the same report of 28 October 2026 give different net passive inflows into Greek equities from the MSCI reclassification of May 2027: about 0.9 billion US dollars in one and about 0.6 billion US dollars in the other.
    • Both passages cite analyst estimates and are tagged to Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley.
    • Morgan Stanley's report of 25 September 2026 gives about 0.9 billion US dollars as the passive inflow into Greece from the STOXX 600 reclassification, and its estimate for OTE alone is net passive inflows of 63 million US dollars.
  12. Deutsche Bank's capital expenditure path.
    • A report of 28 October 2026 says Deutsche Bank sees capital expenditure falling to €550 million in 2029 and €520 million in 2030.
    • Another passage dates a possible fall toward €550 million by 2029 to Deutsche Bank's note of 24 April 2026, after meetings with management.
    • Other passages say Deutsche Bank models a flat €600 million a year through 2028 (reports of 19 June and 27 October 2026) or through 2029 (its work of March 2026, and a report of 14 September 2026 that adds it could fall further after that).

Broker by broker, in date order

Each group is closed; open one to see a dated list, and click a line to jump to its passage. The bold line on each card is a one-line summary; the passage below it is the research report's text, copy-edited. Dates are the date of the broker's view where the research gives one; otherwise the date the report was produced, marked "report of".
